title: scribe-40k Extraction Report
description: Sidecar to a character.json. It records how the document was obtained rather than what it contains: which pages were used, what the models were unsure about, what could not be placed anywhere, and which fields a human still needs to look at. It is a separate document because dark-heresy-character-sheet.schema.json is additionalProperties:false throughout, so provenance cannot be inlined without breaking validation. A character created by hand rather than imported also gets a report, so that consistency flags work the same either way; its 'source' and 'models' are then null.

generatedAt.description: When the extraction ran, in ISO 8601.

filename.description: Original name of the uploaded PDF.

pageCount.description: Pages in the uploaded PDF, including blanks.

source.description: The uploaded PDF, or null for a character created by hand.

oneOf.description: Which models produced this document, so a result can be attributed and reproduced.

models.description: Which models produced this document, or null when none did.

pages.description: Every page of the uploaded PDF and what became of it. Pages are listed even when discarded, so a missing section can be traced back to a page that was blank, unreadable or never matched.

kind.description: 'sheet' matched a template page; 'blank' had no significant ink; 'unrecognised' had content but matched no template page (session notes, a map, a second character).

sheetPage.description: Which of the five printed sheet pages this is. Null unless kind is 'sheet'. Note that this need not equal pdfPage: duplex scans interleave blanks, and pages are often out of order.

textSource.description: 'text_layer' means the PDF carried its own text and no OCR call was made.

matchScore.description: Correlation with the best-matching template page, 0 to 1.

matchedBy.description: Which signal placed this page. 'image' is the page fingerprint. 'text' means the fingerprint could not place it -- a photograph taken at an angle defeats it -- and the page was identified from the printed words its transcription contains instead. 'user' means a person overrode both on the assignment screen.

textScore.description: Weighted share of that sheet page's printed vocabulary found in this page's transcription, 0 to 1. Set only when matchedBy is 'text'.

ink.description: Fraction of dark pixels, used for blank detection.

imagePath.description: Rendered page image, relative to the character directory. Null for blank pages, which are not rendered.

note.description: Why a page was discarded or could not be placed. Shown to the user.

ocrError.description: Populated when transcription failed for this page alone.

flags.description: Everything a human should look at. Each entry addresses one field of the character document by JSON Pointer, so the editor can highlight it in place.

unmapped.description: Content found on the sheet that no field could hold: marginal annotations, arrows, text written outside its box, and pages that are not part of the sheet at all. Surfaced in the editor as an assignment tray rather than discarded, so nothing read from the paper is silently lost.

id.description: Stable identifier, so a dismissal survives a reload.

location.description: Where on the page it sits, in the model's words, e.g. 'left margin beside Demolition'.

reason.description: Why it could not be placed.

status.description: 'assigned' once the user has moved it into a field; 'dismissed' once they have decided it does not belong on the sheet.

assignedTo.description: JSON Pointer the user assigned this to, when status is 'assigned'.

sections.description: One entry per mapping job. Jobs run independently, so a failure here explains why one part of the sheet is empty while the rest is fine.

cached.description: True when the reply came from the local cache rather than a fresh call.

supportsVision.description: Recorded because a text-only reasoning model cannot see ticked boxes, which is most of the data on this sheet. A low skill count from a text-only run is explained by this field.

bbox.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in pixels of the rendered page image, used to crop the evidence shown beside a flagged field.

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into character.json, e.g. '/skills/dodge/proficiency/level'.

severity.description: 'error' means the value is unusable or self-contradictory; 'warning' means it is suspicious but may be deliberate; 'info' is a note.

rule.description: Machine-readable cause, e.g. 'characteristic.total_mismatch' or 'model.low_confidence'. Lets the UI group and the user filter.

message.description: Plain-language explanation shown to the user.

status.description: 'needs_review' until a human acts. 'accepted' means they kept the extracted value as-is; 'user_fixed' means they changed it; 'dismissed' means the flag was wrong.

confidence.description: The model's confidence in this reading, where it gave one.

expected.description: What a consistency rule would have expected.

alternatives.description: Other plausible readings, offered as one-click choices in the editor.

evidence.description: Where on the paper this came from, so the editor can show a crop of the scan beside the field.
